extracted.intended_audience: general readers, journalists, policymakers, and researchers interested in TikTok, platform regulation, and content moderation
extracted.subtask_description: Summarize and enumerate the regulatory, safety, privacy, and moderation-related standards, obligations, and practices discussed in a comprehensive encyclopedic article about TikTok. Covers data residency, child protection, algorithmic risks, security vulnerabilities, and jurisdictional enforcement actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data residency and US oversight (Project Texas)
rubrics_metrics.description: TikTok has been working to silo privileged user data within the United States under oversight from the US government or a third party such as Oracle (named Project Texas).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Project Texas focuses on unauthorized access, state influence, and software security. A new subsidiary, TikTok US Data Security Inc. (USDS), was created to manage user data, software code, back-end systems, and content moderation. It would report to CFIUS, not ByteDance or TikTok; Oracle would review and spot check data flows through USDS, digitally sign software code, approve updates, and oversee content moderation and recommendation. Physical locations would be established so Oracle and the US government could conduct their own reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: European data localization and third‑party oversight (Project Clover)
rubrics_metrics.description: Discussions about 'Project Clover' for storing European information locally and building regional data centres so European data is held in‑region.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plans include building two data centers in Ireland and one in Norway, with a third party overseeing cybersecurity policies, data flows, and personnel access independently of TikTok.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification of 'protected user data' under CFIUS negotiation
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether certain information (e.g., U.S. content creators' data) will remain exempt from being treated as 'protected user data' is being negotiated with CFIUS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This implies a regulatory determination about which data types require special protections and oversight, affecting whether data must be siloed or can be transferred internationally.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data transfer restrictions and GDPR compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: European regulators (Irish Data Protection Commission and others) have investigated and fined TikTok for mishandling children's data and for transfers of personal data to China, citing violations of the GDPR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Relevant expectations include lawful transfers, appropriate safeguards for cross‑border transfers, special protections for children's data, and potential substantial fines for violations (examples cited: €345 million and later €500+ million fines).

rubrics_metrics.name: COPPA compliance and protections for children
rubrics_metrics.description: Collecting information from minors under the age of 13 in violation of the Children's Online Privacy Protection Act (COPPA) led to an FTC consent decree and fines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As a remedial measure, TikTok added a kids‑only mode that blocks upload of videos, building of user profiles, direct messaging, and commenting on others' videos; platforms are expected to implement technical and policy controls to avoid unlawful collection from under‑13s and to comply with consent decrees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Differentiated services and protections for children (GDPR/ICO expectation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulators expect companies to provide different services and different protections for children under data protection law (GDPR/ICO concerns).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The ICO investigation focused on private data collection, the kinds of videos collected and shared by children, and the platform's open messaging system; platforms should design child‑appropriate defaults, limits on features, and parental/guardian protections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Algorithmic transparency and risk disclosure (DSA / EU inquiries)
rubrics_metrics.description: European Commission investigations requested information relating to TikTok's algorithm and risks around elections, mental health, and protection of minors and found violations of digital advertising rules under the DSA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expected practices include providing information about recommendation algorithms to regulators, assessing risks (elections, mental health, minors), and complying with advertising/transparency obligations under the Digital Services Act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Security and patching of software vulnerabilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Security researchers discovered vulnerabilities (e.g., SMS spoofing, in‑app browser code) and tracking behaviors (collection of MAC addresses and IMEIs) that were later patched or disabled.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Platform security criteria include promptly patching exploitable vulnerabilities, avoiding collection of prohibited persistent identifiers per OS policies, disabling suspicious in‑app code (e.g., keylogger functionality) where appropriate, and being transparent about remediation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employee access controls and auditing (journalist data access scandal)
rubrics_metrics.description: Internal investigations found employees had accessed journalists' and their contacts' data to uncover leak sources; employees were fired and the incident investigated by law enforcement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Platforms should limit and audit employee access to user data, log accesses, investigate improper accesses, and take disciplinary and remedial actions where violations occur; regulators may subpoena information and initiate criminal or civil inquiries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Algorithmic safety to prevent 'rabbit holes' and harm amplification
rubrics_metrics.description: Accounts engaging with content related to suicide, self‑harm, or eating disorders were shown more similar videos, creating 'rabbit holes' of recommendations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Platforms are expected to break up such 'rabbit holes', de‑amplify harmful content, and display prompts directing users to mental health resources; algorithms should be tuned to avoid over‑personalizing and repeatedly surfacing self‑harm content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Age‑specific UX safety features (screens limits, notifications curfew)
rubrics_metrics.description: TikTok introduced features like addiction‑reduction prompts (break every 90 minutes), blocking notifications after 9pm/10pm for teens, maximum uninterrupted screen time allowances, default screen time limits for under‑18 users, and dashboards showing usage stats.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Platforms should implement age‑appropriate defaults and controls (e.g., notification curfews, session limits, dashboards) to mitigate excessive use and protect minors' wellbeing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Moderation enforcement against terrorist praise and disallowed content
rubrics_metrics.description: TikTok removed videos praising Hamas and reported removal of hundreds of thousands of videos and thousands of livestreams as part of enforcement actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Content policies should prohibit praise of designated terrorist organizations and other categories of disallowed content; enforcement should be documented, scalable, and responsive to regulator and law‑enforcement requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proactive detection and remediation of sexual exploitation of minors (Kenya case)
rubrics_metrics.description: An investigation found TikTok profited from sexual livestreams involving minors; regulators directed TikTok to remove all sexual content involving minors and to submit a detailed plan to strengthen moderation and child protection systems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Platforms must proactively detect and remove sexual content involving minors, prevent monetization of such content, strengthen moderation systems (including in markets with limited moderation capacity), and provide regulators with remediation plans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monetization/creator program eligibility requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: As of June 2024, requirements for certain monetization programs include account holder being at least 18 years old, having 10,000 followers, and 100,000 views in the last month.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monetization eligibility is enforced via account age, follower and view thresholds and may vary by region; platforms must verify eligibility and ensure minors cannot access monetization in violation of safety rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with consent decrees, investigations and enforcement actions
rubrics_metrics.description: TikTok/ByteDance faced FTC consent decrees, class action settlements, continued investigations, and fines; regulators (FTC, DPC, ICO, European Commission, DOJ) have ongoing inquiries and suits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Platforms are expected to comply with consent decrees, cooperate with investigations, implement required changes, and may face fines, lawsuits, or remedial orders for noncompliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions on platform use on government devices for national security
rubrics_metrics.description: Multiple governments and institutions banned TikTok on government‑issued or staff devices citing cybersecurity and national security concerns (U.S. federal/state bans, EU staff devices banned, army/navy bans).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public‑sector device policies may prohibit certain apps; platforms subject to such policies should provide assurances (e.g., data residency, audits) if they wish to be permitted on government devices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency and regional differences in content visibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Reports that the algorithm hid content depending on user's region (e.g., hiding Palestinian content from users in the Middle East) and accusations of censorship (e.g., of Trump‑critical or Epstein references).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Platforms should be transparent about regional moderation and visibility rules, avoid politically motivated or non‑transparent censorship, and provide explanations and appeal mechanisms for content takedowns or visibility changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advertising rules and digital advertising compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: The European Commission found TikTok violated digital advertising rules under the DSA and launched inquiries into advertising transparency and content aimed at children.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Platforms must comply with advertising transparency rules (disclose paid content, targeting, ads aimed at minors), follow jurisdictional advertising laws, and provide information to authorities on ad practices when required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Workplace practices and employee welfare allegations
rubrics_metrics.description: Allegations of poor workplace conditions, excessive workloads (e.g., employees reporting 85 hours of meetings per week), and EEOC complaints alleging retaliation against workers who complained about discrimination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Companies should maintain reasonable work schedules, ensure lawful workplace practices, investigate discrimination and retaliation complaints, and provide support and flexibility to employees as claimed in corporate responses.
